paper_title: Chart-to-Experience Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Predicting   Experiential Impact of Charts
caption: The task page for crowdsourced online study
model_annotation: Chart-1 displays the share of veterans as a proportion of the total population over time, with data points plotted from 1960 to 2010. The x-axis represents the years, labeled at intervals of 10 years, starting from 1960 and ending at 2010, with a linear scale. The y-axis indicates the percentage of veterans in the population, ranging from 0 to 15%, marked at intervals of 5%, also on a linear scale. A single red line connects data points labeled with specific percentages: 12.8% in 1960, rising to 13.8% in 1970, then decreasing to 12.1% in 1980, 11.0% in 1990, 9.4% in 2000, and finally 7% in 2010. The line shows a peak in 1970 followed by a general decline over the subsequent decades. The source of the data is cited as the Census Bureau, and the chart is attributed to the Pew Research Center.

model_annotations.English: The image displays a task page from a crowdsourced online study, labeled as "Chart-to-Experience Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Predicting Experiential Impact of Charts." The primary visual element is Chart-1, a line graph titled "Veterans as share of population," which illustrates the percentage of veterans in the U.S. population over time. The x-axis represents years, ranging from 1960 to 2010 in ten-year increments, while the y-axis shows the percentage of veterans, scaled from 0% to 15% with major gridlines at 5%, 10%, and 15%. The data, sourced from the Census Bureau and presented by the Pew Research Center, is represented by a red line with circular markers, showing a peak of 13.8% in the early 1970s, followed by a general decline to 7% by 2010. The chart is positioned above a scale for user feedback, where respondents rate the chart's memorability and interest on a five-point scale from "Strongly disagree" to "Strongly agree," with an option to select "Insufficient information to answer." A "Chart Scale" slider is visible in the top-right corner, likely for adjusting the visual presentation of the chart.
